questions.problem:
The matrix $C$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(C).$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}$, where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2},$ and ${c}_{1},$ ${c}_{2}$ are the respective columns of $C.$

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -15\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(C),$ we need to check if the equation $Cx=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[C\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 9 \\ 3 & -3 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=9 \\ 0=12.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get the false statement $0=12.$  

Therefore, the system is inconsistent, which implies that $b\notin \text{Col}(C).$

questions.problem:
The matrix $M$ and the vector $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(M).$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2},$ where ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{m}_{1}+{x}_{2}{m}_{2},$ and ${m}_{1},$  ${m}_{2}$ are the respective columns of $M.$ 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(M),$ we need to check if the equation $Mx=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[M\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[M\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 8 \\ -1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 8 \\ -1 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{2}=8 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives  ${x}_{1}=6.$  

Since we have a solution, the equation $Mx=b$ is consistent, which implies that $b\in \text{Col}(M).$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${m}_{1}$ and ${m}_{2}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}=6\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{m}_{1}}+(-2)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{m}_{2}}
$$

 

Finally, we get ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=6(-2)=-12.$

questions.problem: Consider the matrix given by $A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ k \\ 10\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Col}(A).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(A),$ then the equation $Ax=b$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & -8 \\ 0 & -3 & k \\ 1 & 1 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 10 \\ 0 & -3 & k \\ -5 & 1 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 10 \\ 0 & -3 & k \\ 0 & 6 & 42\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 10 \\ 0 & -3 & k \\ 0 & 0 & 42+2k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=10 \\ -3{x}_{2}=k \\ 0=42+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=42+2k,$ which means that $k=-21.$

$$

$$

Since we have a solution, the equation $Cx=b$ is consistent, which implies that $b\in \text{Col}(C).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${c}_{1},$ ${c}_{2},$ and ${c}_{3}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -12 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}=1\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{1}}+(-5)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{2}}+2\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{3}}
$$

Finally, we get ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=1\cdot (-5)\cdot 2=-10.$

questions.problem:
The matrix $M$ and the vector $b$ are given below.
Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(M).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{m}_{1}+{x}_{2}{m}_{2}+{x}_{3}{m}_{3},$ and ${m}_{1}$, ${m}_{2}$, and ${m}_{3}$ are the respective columns of $M.$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(M),$ we need to check if the equation $Mx=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[M\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[M\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 9 \\ 2 & -2 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 & -24 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 & -24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=9 \\ {x}_{2}=8 \\ {x}_{3}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, from the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+(8) & =9 \\ {x}_{1} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since we have a solution, the equation $Mx=b$ is consistent, which implies that $b\in \text{Col}(M).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${m}_{1},$ ${m}_{2},$ and ${m}_{3}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}=1\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{m}_{1}}+8\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{m}_{2}}+2\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{m}_{3}}
$$

Finally, we get ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=1\cdot 8\cdot 2=16.$

canonical_examples.problem: Consider the matrix given by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064257/assets/7565496e57b9dede7d994f9e8ee936e158f67cc8c7397e182c9c6e940939f823.png) Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064257/assets/b3be9df23c26f562cd1e7c5e1162e87bcc7da0085c00b0185221a6ae45f11395.png) belongs to $\textrm{Col}(A).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Col}(A),$ then the equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ must be consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[A \,|\, \mathbf{b}]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 3 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & -1 & 2+k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & -8 & -32 \\ 5 & -1 & 2+k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & -8 & -32 \\ 0 & -11 & k-48\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -11 & k-48\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+11{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & k-4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=10 \\ {x}_{2}=4 \\ 0=k-4.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for this system to be consistent, we require $0=k-4,$ which means that $k=4.$

canonical_examples.problem:
The matrix $C$ and the vector $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine if $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Col}(C).$ In affirmative case, find the value of $x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot x_3$, where $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ are real numbers such that $\mathbf{b}=x_1\mathbf{c}_1+x_2\mathbf{c}_3+x_3\mathbf{c}_3,$ and $\mathbf{c}_1,$ $\mathbf{c}_2,$ and $\mathbf{c}_3$ are the respective columns of $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064257/assets/ae098d868e48d331a3cf9f73fe0995eadb60c86e1a74eec039b9044592c55a5c.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $\mathbf{b}$ lies in $\textrm{Col}(C),$ we need to check if the equation $C\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[C \,|\, \mathbf{b}]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & 5 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=5 \\ 3{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=1 \\ 5{x}_{3}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=1$. Substituting into the second equation gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2}+4(1) & =1 \\ 3{x}_{2} & =-3 \\ {x}_{2} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, from the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =5-{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3} \\  & =5-(-1)-4(1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we have a solution, the equation $C\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ is consistent, which implies that $\mathbf{b}\in\textrm{Col}(C).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of $\mathbf{c}_1,$ $\mathbf{c}_2,$ and $\mathbf{c}_3\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064257/assets/210497f8b94b3600ef3b784333c7388f65678cd18fb7fdd64f9cc14f0b37c87e.png)

Finally, we get $x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot x_3 = 2 \cdot (-1) \cdot 1 = -2$.
